claims.statement: The repository ships exactly one Poetry package: `sincpro-framework` version 4.0.0, built by `poetry.core.masonry.api` from the single included package `sincpro_framework`, with `fury` (https://pypi.fury.io/sincpro/) declared as a supplemental index.

`poetry.toml` forces an in-project virtualenv (`create = true`, `in-project = true`), and `[tool.pyright]` targets exactly that directory (`venvPath = "."`, `venv = ".venv"`), so type checks resolve against the Poetry-created `.venv`.

The unconditional runtime dependencies are `dependency-injector ^4.49.1` (the IoC container), `pydantic ^2.13.5` (DTO and config base models), `pyyaml >=6.0.1` and `sincpro-log ^1.2.1`, with the declared interpreter range `python = "^3.12"`.

The optional extras map one-to-one onto optional features: `opentelemetry` pulls the OTel API, SDK and both OTLP proto exporters; `sentry` pulls `sentry-sdk`; `mcp` pulls `fastmcp >=3.0,<4`; `rpc` pulls `starlette` and `uvicorn`. Observability and both entrypoint hosts are therefore optional installs while dependency-injector and pydantic are core.

Each optional host imports its library lazily and raises an ImportError whose message names the extra to install: `FASTMCP_MISSING` ends in `pip install sincpro-framework[mcp]` and `RPC_MISSING` in `pip install sincpro-framework[rpc]`.

When the telemetry extras are absent or unconfigured the framework degrades to a recorded status instead of failing: tracing setup returns `off("sdk_missing")` / `off("no_endpoint")` and error reporting returns `off("sdk_missing")` / `off("dsn_missing")`, so the bus keeps executing. The OTLP provider prefers the gRPC exporter and falls back to the HTTP exporter, and the Sentry client is isolated per release without ever calling `sentry_sdk.init()`.

The dev dependency group installs the observability SDKs (all four opentelemetry packages plus sentry-sdk) even though they are optional extras for consumers, so a `poetry install`ed checkout can exercise optional paths without installing an extra — which also means the local suite cannot detect an optional dependency becoming a mandatory one.

The interpreter note in pyproject records a hands-on verification on 3.14.7 / 3.14.7t that every declared dependency installs cleanly on regular (GIL) 3.14 with no code changes and a green test suite, and records free-threading as not implemented or targeted in this codebase.

The free-threaded gap is a dependency-ecosystem gap: on a `python3.14t` interpreter `dependency-injector` (core, required) and `grpcio` (a transitive dependency of the optional `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-grpc`) have no free-threaded wheel, so importing them makes CPython warn and silently re-enable the GIL for the process; `ioc.py` states this is not a bug in this codebase and that regular GIL 3.12/3.13/3.14 are unaffected.

The Makefile is the single entry point for maintainer operations, with `make init` composing `prepare-environment` (pipx installs of poetry/black/autoflake/isort/pyright/pre-commit plus `pre-commit install`) and `install` (`add-gemfury-repo` then `poetry install`).

`make test` runs pytest with `--cov --cov-fail-under=$(COVERAGE_MIN) --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=xml`; `COVERAGE_MIN` defaults to 85 via `?=`, so the coverage floor fails the build when total coverage regresses, while the README still documents "65% by default" — the Makefile value is what executes.

`make verify-format` depends on `format lint`, so it reformats the tree itself and then runs `git diff --quiet`, aborting with the list of changed files; a commit therefore only passes once the reformatted files have been staged, and the failure message is in Spanish.

The pre-commit configuration registers exactly one hook: a local hook whose entry is `make verify-format`, with `language: system`, `pass_filenames: false` and `always_run: true`, installed by `make init`.

Formatting is layered: `autoflake` (in place, removing unused variables/imports, preserving `__init__.py` imports), then `isort`, then `black`, with `line-length = 94` in `[tool.black]`; `format-python` recurses into `format-yaml`, which makes prettier rewrite every `*.yml`/`*.yaml` while yamllint lints only `sincpro_framework/conf/*.yml` and `tests/config/resources/*.yml`.

`.prettierignore` excludes the generated wiki and agent-owned files (`openwiki/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml`) from prettier, and `.yamllint` extends the default ruleset while relaxing only `line-length` (max 100, level warning) plus compatibility switches — `trailing-spaces`, `truthy` and 2-space `indentation` stay enabled.

pyright is the only type checker wired into a gate: `make lint` runs it over `sincpro_framework` and then over `tests`, `[tool.pyright]` pins the venv and disables `reportInvalidTypeVarUse` and `reportInvalidTypeForm`, and `mypy` is declared as a dev dependency but invoked by no Makefile target or workflow step.

The static typing examples are enforced by a test that shells out to pyright: it prefers a `pyright` binary on PATH, otherwise falls back to `poetry run pyright`, and skips when neither executable exists; when it runs, it targets `tests/typing_and_linter/typing_cases` from the repository root and asserts a zero exit code. Consequently a green pytest run is not evidence that types check — `make lint` is the binding gate.

Coverage behaviour lives in pyproject rather than on the command line: `[tool.coverage.run]` measures only the `sincpro_framework` package with branch coverage, `[tool.coverage.report]` enables `show_missing`/`skip_empty` and excludes `TYPE_CHECKING` blocks, `raise NotImplementedError`, `abstractmethod`, `overload` and `__main__` guards, and HTML/XML outputs go to `htmlcov/` and `coverage.xml`.

Pytest's default selection is `testpaths = ["tests"]` and `make test` passes `tests` explicitly; the generated coverage artifacts (`.coverage`, `coverage.xml`, `htmlcov/`) are git-ignored and `make clean-coverage` removes them.

The build and release path is three Makefile targets plus a configuration helper: `update-version` runs `poetry version $(VERSION)` and errors out when `VERSION` is unset; `build` configures the Gemfury index and runs `poetry build`; `publish` configures Gemfury then runs `poetry publish -r fury --build` followed by `poetry publish -u __token__ -p $(POETRY_PYPI_TOKEN)` so one run ships to Gemfury and PyPI.

Release credentials come from Make variables with placeholder defaults (`GEMFURY_PUSH_TOKEN ?= DEFAULT_TOKEN`, `POETRY_PYPI_TOKEN ?= DEFAULT_TOKEN`); `add-gemfury-repo` registers the repository `fury` at https://pypi.fury.io/sincpro/ and `configure-gemfury` sets its http-basic credentials using the token with the password `NOPASS`, with the helper silenced so the token-bearing command is not echoed.

Every GitHub workflow in this repository is a thin caller of a reusable workflow in `Sincpro-SRL/.github` (branch `main`) using `secrets: inherit` and passing only a Python-version list: `02-check_code.yaml` on push with `["3.12", "3.13", "3.14"]`, `03-release_draft.yaml` on push to main with `["3.12"]`, `04-publish_release.yml` on a published release with `["3.12"]`, plus label automation on pull requests and Discord notification. Because the job bodies only delegate, this repository declares the trigger, the Python version and the required secret names, not the build steps.

`04-publish_release.yml` declares `GEMFURY_PUSH_TOKEN` and `POETRY_PYPI_TOKEN` as workflow-level environment from secrets — the same two variable names the Makefile reads — and `02-check_code.yaml` declares `GEMFURY_PUSH_TOKEN` likewise; the local `.yml` file delegates to the org workflow named `.yaml`.

`.github/actions/prepare-env/action.yml` is a composite action taking a Python version input, installing it with `actions/setup-python@v4` and then running `make init`; no workflow in this repository references it, so it is the convention for how a job boots this project rather than a step that runs here today.

Documentation generation is separate from building the package: `make docs` / `docs-init` / `docs-view` are gated by `check-openwiki`, which requires `npx`, Node >= 22 and `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_API_KEY` (or `~/.openwiki/.env`) and otherwise exits with a message naming the missing piece, while the provider, model, endpoint and OpenWiki version are pinned as Make variables. The scheduled `openwiki-update.yml` workflow performs the same job in CI.

The `.PHONY` list at the end of the Makefile is inconsistent with the targets that exist: it names `start`, `clean` and `format-all`, which are not defined, and omits real targets including `lint`, `verify-format`, `test_one`, `update-version` and `publish` — harmless while no same-named files exist.
